items.element: Drag to seat (TASK-344759) — drag-*.html + SeatingPlannerDrag.js
items.current: All four placements from the brief are live: pool → empty seat, pool → table card (first free seat, or refused with "Table full"), seat → seat (move, or swap when the target is occupied), seat → pool (unseat). Plus seat → another table card, which the brief omits but the interaction implies. Drag shows the source dimmed, legal targets in success tone, a "Swap" label on an occupied seat and the refusal reason on a full table. THE SAME FOUR PLACEMENTS RUN BY TAP AND BY KEYBOARD: pick a person, a bar names who is in the air, then choose a seat, a table or the pool; Esc cancels. Nothing re-implements seating — it moves people between card dots and the occupant list and hands off to the shell, so the pool re-derives itself (351550). BUILT IN THE TEMPLATE 2026-09-09 against the data model. All five placements route through ONE place() function so drag and pick-then-place cannot disagree: pool->empty seat, pool->table card (first free seat, or refused '<name> is full' with the person KEPT in the air so you can aim elsewhere), seat->seat (move, or swap when occupied), seat->pool (unseat), and seat->another card. A swap is a single simultaneous exchange, not remove-then-insert — this row already warned that modelling it as delete/insert is how the pair ends up in the same seat. pool->occupied seat is deliberately REFUSED rather than evicting somebody the planner never chose to move; it is not one of the five. AFFORDANCES CORRECTED 2026-09-09. The first pass built them from the description in THIS FIELD — 'legal targets in success tone, a Swap label on an occupied seat' — which describes the PROTOTYPE, not the Figma build, and painted every target green with a Swap pill. The real state already existed: AttendeeCard has a formal State=Dragged Over axis (six variants, one per Type) and .attendee-card--dragged-over was already built, with the component's header naming the parent module as the thing meant to toggle it. Drop targets now carry that class: --ai-surface-minimal background, 1px solid --ai-border-brand, and dashed-to-solid on an empty seat. The Swap pill, the table-card highlight, the tray highlight and the source dimming were all removed — TableCard has twelve variants and NO drag state, Unassigned has no state axis, and the component is designer-confirmed as never being a drag source. A table card and the tray are still functional drop targets with no highlight. SECOND CORRECTION, same day: the first fix used the right class but applied it to EVERY LEGAL SEAT, lighting most of the list. The state is named Dragged OVER — it means the one card under the pointer, not a card you could legally drop on. That was the prototype's 'legal targets in success tone' framing surviving into a second attempt at the same feature. It is now applied by markOver() from dragover/dragleave for the drag path and mouseover/focusin for the click and keyboard paths, exactly one card at a time, still gated by legality so an illegal target never promises a drop that place() refuses.
items.needs: Each placement is a TableSeat write — occupant plus seat order. A SWAP is two rows changing in ONE transaction, or the pair can end up in the same seat; a move between tables changes the parent Table too, so it must not be modelled as delete-then-insert. Re-read the plan after a placement rather than trusting the client, since two editors can aim at the same seat. FRONT-END GAP, needs a designer decision, not code: a table card and the tray accept a drop and show nothing, because neither component has a drag state in Figma. Two other visuals have no Figma counterpart — the 'in the air' bar (kept as a WCAG floor, since a keyboard user cannot drag and needs to perceive the mode change) and seat rows being draggable at all, which sits against AttendeeCard's designer-confirmed 'never a drag source'.

items.element: Placing a person without drag — the touch and keyboard path
items.current: The brief asks how this works on mobile. It is not a separate mobile feature: pick-then-place is the mechanism and drag is an accelerator for it. Tap (or Enter) a person in the pool or a seated row to pick them up — a fixed bar names them and offers Cancel — then tap a seat, a table card or the pool to place them. Esc or Cancel aborts. Rows carry tabindex, so the whole flow works from the keyboard, which matters because keyboard users cannot drag either. Verified in a browser: pick, place, swap, unseat, cancel and refusal all work by tap and by Enter, and picking does not hijack table selection. BUILT IN THE TEMPLATE 2026-09-09, and built as the PRIMITIVE rather than as a fallback: click or Enter picks a person up, a fixed bar names them and offers Cancel, then a click or Enter on a seat, a table card or the tray places them; Esc puts them down. Drag is wired on top of the same place() call, so it is genuinely an accelerator. A guard stops a card click changing the table SELECTION while somebody is in the air — without it, aiming at a table silently just re-selected it. PICK BAR CORRECTED 2026-09-10. Its Cancel button was unreachable during a pointer drag — the button is already down, and releasing ends the drag and clears the pick anyway — so it advertised an action the user could not take in the one mode where they did not need it. Cancel is now shown only for click-and-keyboard picks (`pick(src, viaDrag)` records how the pick began); during a drag the bar is pure status. Two more fixes alongside: Escape now cancels a pick by either route, with an open dialog still winning precedence — it previously did not cancel a pick at all, despite being the reflex key for a held item; and the `role="status" aria-live="polite"` moved from the wrapper to the message, since a live region announces changes rather than hosting controls and a screen reader may read it without reliably exposing the button. The bar has no Figma counterpart — it is the accessibility floor for the placement path a keyboard user has to use.

The two other alternatives, the compare board, the layout switcher, its demo bar and the four old fallback workspace states have been deleted; workspace.html is the only workspace file. Shape: tables list | table detail | unassigned, each region owning its own scroller so the PAGE never scrolls and both ends of a drag stay on screen — the defect this replaced put the pool's first row at y~1013 in a page-scrolled 1356px document, so you could see the seats or the pool but never both. (1) The Unassigned sheet overflowed the row: the component had no height treatment at all, so it grew to its 72-person content — it now fills its column and scrolls its list, the same treatment TableDetail carries, with `flex-shrink: 0` on the list's children because a height-constrained flex column otherwise squashes every row to ~1px. items.current: Rebuilt as two rows: the title with New plan and Copy plans to event on one line, the rooms beneath on their own horizontally scrollable line. Desktop gets prev/next ARROWS instead of a scrollbar — hidden until the rooms overflow, and each hides again at its end, so a visible arrow always does something. Touch gets a swipe with no arrow. The room cards KEEP their size-4 (240px) width below 1024 rather than stretching to fill the track, so the cut card at the edge is emergent rather than guaranteed: measured with five plans, a card is cut at 500, 560, 600, 700, 768 and 900px (10% to 97% of a card showing), but at ~527, ~775 and 1023px the cards land exactly flush (track = 248n - 8) and nothing would signal the rest. The pill is presentational: it owns no show/hide, no auto-dismiss timer and no JS at all — unlike the `Toast` card, it has no close button to wire. `role="status"` (Success) and `role="alert"` (Error) are in place, so a screen reader announces it once it is inserted. WIRED INTO THE DS TEMPLATE 2026-09-09 for table create and edit, from Figma 1:6763 (edited) and 1:6881 (added) in the Seating Planner file. The open question this entry recorded — "who retires a toast" — is now answered: auto-dismiss after 4s (8s when first wired on 2026-09-09, shortened the same day at the designer's request), the timer PAUSES while the pointer is over the pill or focus is inside it so Undo cannot expire mid-read or mid-tab (the WCAG 2.2 concern this entry raised), Esc dismisses, one toast at a time. The host is a fixed, click-through, viewport-centred region 24px off the bottom; only the pill takes pointer events. Both frames place the toast identically (465x58 at x=632 y=1033 in 1728x1117), i.e. centred with a 26px gap — built at --ai-spacing-6 (24px) because 26 maps to no token (designer). Raised via a `sp:toast` CustomEvent, so the raising code needs no load-order guarantee and nothing new lands on `window`. The pill built by JS deliberately omits the `role="status"` the component demo shows: the HOST is the live region, present from load, because a freshly-inserted status element announces unreliably. COPY: both frames emphasise SUBJECT and OBJECT with a plain verb between — "**Table 13** added to **Main Ballroom.**" and "**Table 1** renamed to **Headline Sponsors**". The punctuation differs between them (full stop inside the bold on add, none on rename) and is reproduced as drawn. A third case is not drawn at all — an edit that changes capacity/tier/sponsor/host but not the name — and reads "**Table 2** updated", since "renamed to" would be false there. MEASURED DISCREPANCY, pre-existing and NOT introduced by this wiring: the pill renders 60px tall against Figma's 58. This file's own comment computes 58 as 1+12+32+12+1, assuming a 32px CTA, but `.btn--xs` is 32px of padding+line-height PLUS a 1px border each side, so the CTA is 34 and the pill is 60. Left alone rather than retuning a component signed off on 2026-08-26 from a screen-level task — worth a designer call on whether the CTA or the pill padding should give. DELETE TOAST ADDED 2026-09-09 from Figma 1:43029 desktop / 1:44173 mobile, and it is Type=ERROR rather than success — both frames place `Icon/24px/TriangleAlert` with the --ai-border-error ring where the create and edit toasts place BadgeCheck and the success ring. A removal is reported as a warning. The toast module now takes a `type` in its `sp:toast` detail ('success' | 'error') and picks the modifier and the icon from it, so the two Types the component already had are both in use. Copy keeps the bold-subject / plain-verb / bold-object shape: "**Table 2** has been removed from **Main Ballroom.**", full stop inside the emphasis as with the add toast. Undo restores the card AT ITS ORIGINAL POSITION — the next sibling's id is part of the snapshot, because re-appending would drop a restored table at the end of the grid and table order is how people find them; verified by deleting a middle card and getting the order 1..12 back intact. MOBILE TYPE STEP-DOWN added to the COMPONENT (SeatingToast.css): 13px/16 against the base 14px/20, read off 1:44212 — the file's only mobile toast frame — and confirmed by its get_variable_defs (--ai-font-fixed-2xs 13, --ai-leading-xs 16); the paired desktop toast 1:43089 keeps 14/20, so it is a real breakpoint change. It applies to EVERY toast, not just delete: there is no mobile frame for create or edit, but the step-down is a property of the component at that width rather than of one message, and a delete toast a size smaller than a create toast on the same phone would be the odd outcome. Flagged on that basis. Two positional notes, neither acted on: the delete frames place the toast 44px off the bottom where the create/edit frames use 26px, and the mobile delete frame centres it on the CONTENT COLUMN (x=64 in a 402 frame, right of the 52px sidebar) rather than the viewport — the host uses one viewport-centred 24px offset for all toasts, since three hand-placed offsets across frames read as Figma noise. items.needs: **Undo is still the part that needs the backend.** It is now WIRED but DOM-only: the toast carries a snapshot of exactly what that one save touched (the card's outerHTML, the plan totals, the seat panel and the selection) and restores it. items.element: css/tokens-cc.css — --ai-btn-tertiary-bg, and every tertiary button on every Control Centre screen
items.current: LIKELY A SHIFTED RAMP IN THE CC MODE, reported by the designer via the Room Layout trash button. --ai-btn-tertiary-bg is rgba(0,0,0,0) in tokens.css, tokens-dark.css, tokens-chat.css and tokens-chat-dark.css, but #e5e9eb in tokens-cc.css — so tertiary buttons paint a grey box at rest throughout the Control Centre. The CC trio is rest #e5e9eb / hover #f2f4f5 / pressed #e5e9eb: rest and pressed are the SAME value and hover is LIGHTER than both, so hovering pales the button and pressing returns it to rest — the affordance is inverted. Read as transparent -> #f2f4f5 -> #e5e9eb the ramp matches every other mode exactly, which points at the rest slot having been given the pressed value. Worked around for now by overriding ONLY the rest state on Room Layout's two remove buttons, scoped, so hover/pressed/focus still come from the component and the override lapses once the token is fixed.

Then delete the scoped override in SeatingPlanner.css. Worth checking the other CC screens for tertiary buttons carrying the same grey box. items.element: The working prototype's data model — src/cc/templates/SeatingPlanner/seating-data.js
items.current: IN-MEMORY, resets on reload (designer's choice, so every demo starts from the same baseline). Built from the Design System 'Populated' frames 3515:202250 / 3515:213496. Four plans (Main Ballroom 13 tables, Overflow Annex 6, VIP Lounge 4, Press Room 3), a 183-person roster, and a seat-level assignment per table. AUTHORED: the plans, tables, each table's type and sponsor, and who sits in which seat. DERIVED by seating-app.js and never stored: occupancy, the per-role legend split, plan totals, seats free, the unassigned pool and the event's attendee figure. UNASSIGNED = SIGNED UP MINUS ASSIGNED, event-wide, and unrelated to capacity (designer: 'there could be 3000 seats available but only 80 people signed up, and 10 have been assigned so 70 are unassigned'). The roster is 183 rather than the frame's 386 because 386 signed up with 72 unassigned needs 314 people seated and the four plans hold 234 — so the attendee figure is derived from the roster, being a moving variable by the same rule. The people are GENERATED mock names, deterministic by index so the baseline is identical on every load.

Derive every count server-side for the same reason it is derived here — a stored count is the thing that drifts. Note the roster here is mock: see seating-export-occupant-coverage.

items.element: Why picking somebody up decorates instead of re-rendering — seating-app.js pick()/undecorate()
items.current: A REAL BUG, found and fixed during the drag build. pick() originally called render(), which rebuilds the listing and the detail with innerHTML. On dragstart that detaches the very element being dragged, so the browser had nothing to drag and no drop event ever fired; worse, dragend also fired on the detached node, so `picked` stayed set and the NEXT ordinary click was silently treated as a placement. Picking somebody up changes no data, so it now only decorates, with an undecorate() kept beside decoratePick() — a mark added in one and not removed in the other survives as a permanently highlighted row.
items.needs: Nothing server-side. Worth knowing if the renderer is ever changed to re-render more eagerly: any innerHTML rebuild during a drag will break the drag. Raised by this build.

items.element: Drag-over feedback that has no Figma state — table card, unassigned tray, picked source, the "in the air" bar
items.current: AttendeeCard is the ONLY component in this flow with a drag state (State=Dragged Over, six variants), and it is used. The other targets and the source have none, so after the 2026-09-09 correction they carry no highlight at all: a table card and the tray accept a drop and say nothing, and the picked person is not marked. The 'in the air' bar is kept regardless, because pick-then-place is a keyboard user's only path and an imperceptible mode change fails WCAG 2.1 — but it is unspecified too. Nothing here is invented any more; the gaps are visible as gaps. TABLE CARD RESOLVED 2026-09-10: dragging over a table card now takes the SELECTED state's styling, at the designer's direction — `.table-card--drop-target` shares the `--selected` rule rather than copying it, so the two cannot drift. A separate class deliberately: the selected table is a persistent choice driving the detail rail and carrying `aria-pressed="true"`, while a drop target is momentary; reusing the class would make them indistinguishable in the DOM and put aria-pressed on a card nobody pressed. NOT a new variant — Figma still has no drag state for TableCard, and pointing at an existing variant's styling is the designer resolving the gap rather than an invention (the earlier `--drop-legal`/`--drop-full` attempt was removed for being exactly that). Legality gates it as it does for seats: only the card under the pointer, and `tableDrop()`'s 'full' is excluded because place() refuses it. STILL OPEN: the unassigned tray as a drop target shows nothing, and seat rows remain `draggable` against AttendeeCard's designer-confirmed "never a drag source". TRAY RESOLVED 2026-09-10, so both drop surfaces now show state. The tray takes `.unassigned--drop-target`. Unlike TableCard there was no state axis to point at — Unassigned has two variants and both are Type — so the values come from the system's established drop-target pair, `--ai-border-brand` on `--ai-surface-minimal`, designer-confirmed for AttendeeCard's `--dragged-over` and shared by TableCard's drop target. An approved pair rather than two invented values, but still a treatment Figma does not draw for Unassigned. Gated by `poolDrop()`, which is null for a pool source since pool→pool is a no-op; hovering one of the tray's own rows marks the TRAY, which is right because a drop anywhere in it unseats. THE `draggable` QUESTION IS CLOSED AS A NON-ISSUE: AttendeeCard's "drop target only… the card never initiates a drag" constrains the COMPONENT — no drag JS in its own files — and explicitly hands the drag to the parent module, which is exactly what happens (the attribute is set by the Seating Planner on its own instances, every dragstart handler is in seating-app.js). Reading it verbatim, there was no contradiction to fix; the earlier flag overstated it. AttendeeCard's notes now spell the division out so the next reader does not hit the same apparent conflict. HIGHLIGHT STICKINESS FIXED 2026-09-10: the tray's drop highlight stayed lit after the drop. Two causes. (1) `finish()` set `state.picked = null` directly, clearing the pick's data but not its decoration — `render()` had been doing that cleanup BY ACCIDENT, because it rebuilds the listing and seat rows via innerHTML so any class on those went out with the element; the tray sheet is authored markup that survives a render, making it the first decoration to stay lit. `finish()` now calls `clearPick()`, which also stops `state.pickedViaDrag` leaking from the same line. (2) The highlight keyed on `[data-sp-pool-region]` while dragover/drop/click keyed on `[data-sp-pool]`, the sheet inside it — they coincide in today's layout, but a drop the handler does not recognise never calls place() and so never clears anything, which is exactly the reported shape. All four now use the region.
items.needs: Designer decisions: (1) a Dragged Over state for TableCard, whose axes today are State (Default | Selected) x Type (Empty | Populated | Full) x Device with no drag state; (2) the same for Unassigned, which has only empty and populated variants; (3) how a picked-up person should read, given AttendeeCard is confirmed as never a drag source yet seat->seat move and swap require dragging one; (4) a designed counterpart for the in-the-air bar. Raised by this build.
